clue.text: "X" has powerful following that can be maintained

indicators.note: following says the next piece comes straight after the one before it

blocks.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten
able in the sense of strong or capable

explanation.surface: Something marked X has a strong follow-up that can be kept going.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks around X invite reading it as a Roman numeral rather than a letter or a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenable position is one capable of being held or defended, a straightforward adjective synonym.

clue.text: Enjoy a sumptuous meal before parting

blocks.note: to ... is to eat well, read as two words
a goodbye, as a noun or adjective

explanation.surface: A lavish last supper before people go their separate ways.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as FARE WELL it means to dine well; as one word it is a goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: A farewell is a leave-taking, so parting words or a parting gift are farewell ones.

clue.text: The badly-bred one's trash!

indicators.note: something done badly is done wrongly, so the letters are put out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
one is I, and one's becomes I's, written IS

explanation.surface: A snobbish sneer that an ill-bred person's belongings are rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly-bred' reads as one word for a lout, but badly is the anagram signal working on bred.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is scattered rubbish or remains, so it is a synonym of trash as a noun.

clue.text: A member gets nothing in the break after all

indicators.note: one thing set inside another is placed in it

blocks.note: a rest is a break from work
an arm is a limb, a member of the body
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone joins but gains nothing during the interval in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After all' looks like a phrase meaning in the end, but it is the definition: behind all the others.
explanation.definitionFit: Rearmost means furthest back, the one coming last after every other in a line.

clue.text: Correct concerning fashion

blocks.note: re means about or concerning, as in a letter heading
to form is to fashion or shape

explanation.surface: A pedantic remark that something is proper with regard to style.
explanation.definitionFit: To reform is to put right or improve, so it is a verb synonym of correct.

clue.text: Study neat model - it's only natural

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so the letters that follow are reshaped

blocks.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
the letters of neat, rearranged

explanation.surface: Examining a tidy model, someone remarks that it looks perfectly natural.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like a noun being studied, but it is a verb telling you to reshape neat.
explanation.definitionFit: Connate means inborn or innate, a quality that comes naturally from birth.

clue.text: Offered an account that might have been altered

indicators.note: suggests the word could have been put together in another order

blocks.note: its seven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone told a story that may have been doctored.
explanation.walkthrough: The word altered itself supplies the letters, which is a neat touch since it means changed.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate a story is to narrate it, so having related means having told or given an account.

clue.text: Grow a number in running water, then cut

indicators.note: one item placed inside another is in it

blocks.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and another in Wales and England
V is the Roman numeral five
to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: Instructions for raising something in flowing water and then pruning it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running water' is a river, and the Dee, in Scotland and in Wales, is a favourite crossword river.
explanation.definitionFit: To develop is to grow or evolve into something larger or more mature.

clue.text: American beggars having food to cook?

blocks.note: first meaning: US slang for people who beg on the street
second meaning, whimsical: cooks who hold the handles of their saucepans

explanation.surface: Wondering whether street beggars in America have anything to cook.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as PAN HANDLERS, the word describes cooks gripping their pans; the question mark flags this playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To panhandle is American slang for begging in the street, so beggars there are panhandlers.

clue.text: Calling for private transport always

blocks.note: a car is a private vehicle
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever

explanation.surface: Someone forever phoning for their own taxi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Calling' suggests shouting or phoning, but it is the noun meaning vocation.
explanation.definitionFit: A calling is a vocation or profession, which is what a career is.

clue.text: Music tolerated when flying

blocks.note: an air is a tune
borne is the past participle of bear, to put up with

explanation.surface: In-flight music that passengers put up with.
explanation.definitionFit: Airborne describes an aircraft or bird in the air, aloft rather than on the ground.

clue.text: In the jungle each new plant discovered brings joy

indicators.note: says the letters sit inside the words that follow
something discovered is uncovered from within, so a run of letters is found there

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of jungle and start of each
surface filler, the new plant the explorer discovers

explanation.surface: Every new plant an explorer finds in the jungle is a thrill.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles two words: junGLE Each.
explanation.definitionFit: Glee is great delight or happiness, a noun synonym for joy.

clue.text: He's too calm, maybe, for a young peer

indicators.note: suggests the words are one possible arrangement among others

blocks.note: the ten letters of these words, rearranged

explanation.surface: Commenting that a youngster is unusually composed for an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' suggests a member of the nobility, but here it means an equal of the same age.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer is an equal, and a young one sharing your classes is a schoolmate.

clue.text: Taking turns to fix a race

blocks.note: to alter is to change or adjust
a nation is a people or race

explanation.surface: Taking turns at rigging a horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fix a race' looks like race-rigging; race here means a people.
explanation.definitionFit: Alternation is the act of going back and forth by turns, so taking turns is alternation.

clue.text: English working men, made redundant, snarled

indicators.note: working suggests the parts being moved around into a new arrangement

blocks.note: E is the standard abbreviation for English
the letters of men, rearranged
to shed staff is to lay them off

explanation.surface: English workers, on losing their jobs, growled angrily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snarled' looks like an angry growl, but it is the sense of tangled.
explanation.definitionFit: Snarled can mean tangled up or caught, which is what enmeshed means.

clue.text: Where one may raise fruit or vegetables

blocks.note: taken as written
chard is a leafy green vegetable

explanation.surface: A gardening note on places to grow fruit or vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruit or vegetables' reads as one list, but the definition stops at fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Orchards are plots of fruit trees, places where fruit is grown and harvested.

clue.text: Perception of the popular view

blocks.note: in means fashionable or popular
a sight is a view or spectacle

explanation.surface: How the public sees things.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is the power of seeing into a situation, a deep understanding or discernment.

clue.text: Rules to be observed about a German analgesic

indicators.note: about suggests turning around, so the following letters are moved about

blocks.note: a code is a set of rules to follow
ein is German for a, here rearranged

explanation.surface: Regulations to be followed regarding a German painkiller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A German' asks for the German word for a, EIN, whose letters are then moved about.
explanation.definitionFit: Codeine is an opiate drug used to relieve pain, so it is an analgesic.

clue.text: Advise partner in a friendly way

blocks.note: to inform is to tell or advise
an ally is a partner

explanation.surface: Tell your colleague something in a relaxed, friendly manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally means casually, without ceremony, which suits a relaxed and friendly manner.

clue.text: A predatory bird's large kill

blocks.note: OS is the abbreviation for outsize
an animal's kill is its prey

explanation.surface: A bird of prey's sizeable catch.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for is, joining definition and wordplay. OS means outsize, a clothing size.
explanation.definitionFit: The osprey is a fish-eating hawk, a bird of prey that dives for its catch.

clue.text: The one-time warning given by the farming community

blocks.note: ye is an old spelling of the, as in Ye Olde Shoppe
an omen is a portent or warning sign

explanation.surface: A historical alert issued by country folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One-time' means formerly, pointing to an archaic form of the.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeomen were small landowning farmers in England, so collectively they were the farming class.

clue.text: The firm with little work is to shut up

blocks.note: Co is the abbreviation for company
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A company with too little business is about to close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shut up' looks like closing down, but it means confine, as hens are.
explanation.definitionFit: To coop up is to confine in a small space, like chickens kept in a cage or pen.

clue.text: Just the man to deal with the underworld problem!

definitions.text: Just the man to deal with

blocks.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and its name
a poser is a puzzling problem

explanation.surface: A fixer who can sort out a gangland difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld' suggests organised crime, but it is the classical land of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A disposer is one who disposes of things, that is, who deals with or gets rid of them.

clue.text: An ass over gear-changing

indicators.note: changing means altering, so the word's letters are swapped around

blocks.note: on can mean over or upon, as in a lid on a box
the letters of gear rearranged

explanation.surface: A donkey being silly about changing gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' gives ON, in the sense of resting upon something.
explanation.definitionFit: An onager is a wild ass of Asia, so it is a specific kind of ass.

clue.text: They invariably take the first lady into this

indicators.note: one thing taken into another ends up inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
Eve was the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: Robbers always drag the President's wife into the scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First lady' suggests a President's wife, but means the first woman of Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: Thieves are people who steal, so taking things is their invariable habit.

clue.text: Making some advance, left before the finish

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
an ending is a finish

explanation.surface: Making progress, but quitting just before the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advance' suggests progress, but it is a loan of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Lending is giving a loan, and an advance is money lent ahead of time.
